title: Conditionals: `if`, `if-else` with an initialiser and `switch` without fall-through

videos.script: Lesson 18 was about leaving a loop early. This lesson is about choosing between paths. {{if}} Go's if looks like the one you know, with three differences. There are no parentheses around the condition. The braces are never optional. And else sits on the same line as the closing brace, for a reason the compiler will show you. {{init}} An if can also begin with a short statement of its own, very often a call that returns an error. The names it declares live inside the if and its else branches, and nowhere else. {{switch}} Then switch. In Go, a case does not run on into the next one. Each case ends by itself, one case can list several values, and a switch with no value at all replaces a long chain of else ifs. {{fallthrough}} For the rare time you want the old behaviour, a keyword asks for it out loud. By the end, you will write each choice in the shape a Go reader expects.
